role: DIFFERENTIATED_SUPPORT: independent retrieval, selected guided reteach, fresh independent retry and extension. Cross-curricular role, not a new subject. ENGLISH is an allowed recorded carrier from the grade day, per CoS ROLE_CONTRACTS.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: The digits of a factor are multiplied as single units and their products are added.
targetedPaths.activity: Represent 312 as 300, 10 and 2. Multiply each full value by 3 before combining.
hints: Name the full place values before multiplying: 2 hundreds is 200, not 2.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Find 214 times 4. Explain the value of each digit.
targetedPaths.feedback: Name the full place values before multiplying: 2 hundreds is 200, not 2.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: Tens or hundreds formed by a partial product are discarded when writing the final digits.
targetedPaths.activity: Trade ten ones for one ten without throwing away value. Show how 4 times 4 ones becomes one ten and six ones.
hints: Keep the value of every partial product and regroup it into the correct place rather than deleting it.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Find 214 times 4 and explain where the regrouped ten goes.
targetedPaths.feedback: Keep the value of every partial product and regroup it into the correct place rather than deleting it.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: The swallowed food route is drawn through the liver or pancreas instead of distinguishing the juices they supply.
targetedPaths.activity: Use one arrow for swallowed food and different arrows for digestive juices. Place liver and pancreas beside the food route.
hints: Keep the continuous food route separate from the liver and pancreas, which supply digestive juices.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Trace food to the small intestine and explain one supporting organ.
targetedPaths.feedback: Keep the continuous food route separate from the liver and pancreas, which supply digestive juices.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: The stomach is treated as the place where all nutrients enter the body.
targetedPaths.activity: Compare the stomach with the small intestine. Locate where most digested nutrients enter the body.
hints: Most digested nutrients are absorbed through the small-intestine wall.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Explain why the food route continues beyond the stomach.
targetedPaths.feedback: Most digested nutrients are absorbed through the small-intestine wall.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: Nutrients that cross the wall are treated as disappearing from the model total.
targetedPaths.activity: Move paper nutrient tokens into a body region while keeping every token visible. Transferred tokens still exist.
hints: Keep transferred tokens visible in the body region. Count both regions to conserve the total.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Start with 16 tokens. Transfer 6. Explain where all 16 are now.
targetedPaths.feedback: Keep transferred tokens visible in the body region. Count both regions to conserve the total.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: The starting count is reported as still inside after tokens have crossed the wall.
targetedPaths.activity: Label the starting total before moving tokens. Label the tokens still in the first region separately.
hints: The starting count describes both regions together. Subtract transferred tokens to find what remains inside.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Start with 16 and transfer 6. Find and distinguish the starting and remaining counts.
targetedPaths.feedback: The starting count describes both regions together. Subtract transferred tokens to find what remains inside.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: The number transferred during a round is confused with the number remaining inside.
targetedPaths.activity: Keep transferred and remaining tokens in two labelled groups. Point to the group named by each question.
hints: Transferred and remaining name different groups. Track the inside count after every transfer.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Start with 16 and transfer 6. Find the transferred and remaining counts and explain the difference.
targetedPaths.feedback: Transferred and remaining name different groups. Track the inside count after every transfer.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: A plausible prediction is reported as something the story has already established.
targetedPaths.activity: Mark an early clue, your prediction and a later detail in the accepted reading text. Treat the prediction as a possibility.
hints: Name the detail that makes the idea plausible, use might or may, and change the prediction if later evidence conflicts.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Name an unanswered question from the text without inventing an ending.
targetedPaths.feedback: Name the detail that makes the idea plausible, use might or may, and change the prediction if later evidence conflicts.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: A summary lists incidental details or invents an outcome instead of connecting the central problem, response and result.
targetedPaths.activity: Choose details that explain the main problem, response and result. Put minor details aside.
hints: Keep the problem, the action taken and the result supported by the story; remove details that do not explain that connection.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Summarize the text and justify one detail you kept.
targetedPaths.feedback: Keep the problem, the action taken and the result supported by the story; remove details that do not explain that connection.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: Every inland location is assumed to be high or mountainous.
targetedPaths.activity: Separate coastal or inland labels from evidence about elevation or a particular route. Use the accepted records.
hints: Inland means away from the coast. A broad terrain description does not determine every local elevation.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Explain what further observation would support a claim about one site.
targetedPaths.feedback: Inland means away from the coast. A broad terrain description does not determine every local elevation.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: One observation or place description is treated as evidence about all communities.
targetedPaths.activity: Compare what the two club records actually describe. One record does not describe every place.
hints: Name the place and observation, limit the conclusion to that evidence and seek additional observations.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Give a conditional recommendation and state one limit of the records.
targetedPaths.feedback: Name the place and observation, limit the conclusion to that evidence and seek additional observations.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: Coastal or inland is treated as enough evidence to select a safe site.
targetedPaths.activity: Match each room or route claim to its actual observation. A place name does not establish safety.
hints: Compare the actual site, path and local observations. A region label alone does not establish safety.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Identify a missing observation before deciding whether a site meets a need.
targetedPaths.feedback: Compare the actual site, path and local observations. A region label alone does not establish safety.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: General coast-to-inland landform descriptions are treated as exact county boundaries.
targetedPaths.activity: Use separate labels for a physical region and an administrative county. They answer different kinds of questions.
hints: Use an administrative map for county boundaries. A physical sketch does not establish those lines.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Explain why a coastal label is not by itself the name of a county.
targetedPaths.feedback: Use an administrative map for county boundaries. A physical sketch does not establish those lines.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: Evidence about a dry room or a clear path is treated as proving the other requirement too.
targetedPaths.activity: Make separate columns for room conditions and route access. Check each need with relevant evidence.
hints: Check each requirement separately. Room and route observations answer different questions.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Explain how a dry room could still be reached by a difficult route.
targetedPaths.feedback: Check each requirement separately. Room and route observations answer different questions.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: The variable's name is changed whenever its number changes.
targetedPaths.activity: Keep the score name card fixed and replace only the number card when its value changes.
hints: Keep the name score fixed and replace the number stored beneath it.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Start score at 2 and add 3. Explain what changes and what stays fixed.
targetedPaths.feedback: Keep the name score fixed and replace the number stored beneath it.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: Set score to a number is treated as adding that number.
targetedPaths.activity: Compare set to 2 with add 2 from the same starting score of 4. Set replaces; add uses the previous value.
hints: Set replaces the current value. Add uses the current value to calculate the next one.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Start at 1. Add 3, set to 2, then add 3. Explain every state.
targetedPaths.feedback: Set replaces the current value. Add uses the current value to calculate the next one.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: Initialization is repeated before every event, discarding the accumulated score.
targetedPaths.activity: Initialize at the start of a new game. Keep the updated value between hits unless a reset event occurs.
hints: Initialize at new-game start and retain the updated value between events.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Start at 0 and add 2 for each of three hits. Explain why resetting before every hit loses the total.
targetedPaths.feedback: Initialize at new-game start and retain the updated value between events.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: A set instruction is ignored and the previous value is retained.
targetedPaths.activity: Follow every instruction in order, including set. Replace the number even when no points were earned.
hints: Follow every instruction in order. Set replaces the old value even if no points were earned.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Start at 7, set to 2, then add 3. Record all three states.
targetedPaths.feedback: Follow every instruction in order. Set replaces the old value even if no points were earned.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: A new game starts without initialization and inherits an earlier game's score.
targetedPaths.activity: Show the end of one game and the starting value of a new game on separate cards. Initialize the new game.
hints: Give each new game its stated starting value before processing events.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: One game ends at 9. A new game starts at 0. Explain the new score before its first hit.
targetedPaths.feedback: Give each new game its stated starting value before processing events.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: The switch creates the energy that lights the lamp.
targetedPaths.activity: Sketch the battery, lamp and conducting return path. Open and close the switch on the sketch.
hints: The battery supplies energy. Closing the switch completes a conducting path; the switch does not create energy.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Explain why closing a switch does not create energy.
targetedPaths.feedback: The battery supplies energy. Closing the switch completes a conducting path; the switch does not create energy.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: One successful test proves the switch always works.
targetedPaths.activity: Read every actual or explicitly supplied trial from the accepted Engineering activity. Include failures and identify the source.
hints: Record every trial, including failures. Five trials support a limited comparison, not a guarantee.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Explain what five trials support and what they do not guarantee.
targetedPaths.feedback: Record every trial, including failures. Five trials support a limited comparison, not a guarantee.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: Changing several components establishes which single change caused an outcome.
targetedPaths.activity: Name one contact feature to change. Keep battery, lamp, wires and procedure fixed.
hints: Change one contact feature while keeping battery, bulb, wires and procedure fixed.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Propose a further test and explain which conditions you will keep fixed.
targetedPaths.feedback: Change one contact feature while keeping battery, bulb, wires and procedure fixed.

targetedPaths.diagnosticDescription: The taller closed-switch bar proves the best design without checking open-switch control.
targetedPaths.activity: Read both closed-light bars, then inspect both open-dark counts. Both criteria matter.
hints: Use both closed-light and open-dark observations, and acknowledge the limits of the tests.
Keep your first attempt. Explain how the evidence or representation changes your reasoning.
targetedPaths.freshRetry: Use available records to justify a choice. Without data, explain a plan only.
targetedPaths.feedback: Use both closed-light and open-dark observations, and acknowledge the limits of the tests.

selection: Six retrieval prompts cover the six periods. Use the actual response to select relevant cards with the learner. Cards are passive reference material, not 23 mandatory lessons. The teacher chooses a path; no automatic adaptive router is claimed.
misconceptionScope: Each of the 23 accepted source misconceptions has a specifically attributed activity, guidance and retry card. The candidate declares two cross-cutting support misconceptions; source IDs on cards remain source references, not machine diagnoses or mastery updates.
independentBoundary: Do not open guidance before the first attempt. Offer the matching fresh question without worked guidance; oral explanations or pupil-directed scribing are valid. A lesson not attempted is not a deficit.
access: Read the selected card aloud; use paper, counters, labels and oral/scribed responses. No dragging, color, typing speed or network dependency. Keep examples separate from independent evidence.
timing: 20 minutes is proposed, not measured. Use brief oral retrieval and one relevant card/retry; do not require every card or extension. Rehearsal remains a gate.
extension: Offer the counterexample task when the teacher judges readiness from the work. Learners needing more practice explain their next relevant step instead; no self-declared mastery trigger.
engineering: Preserve group-kit safety and rotation from P6. No kit or approved dataset is supplied here. Distinguish performed tests, group observation, analysed provided observations and sketch-only work.
assessment: Formative only. No official grades, record writes, persistence or automatic mastery/diagnostic claims.
